subject: TTFT / streaming cadence — FinHub production targets & handoff
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finhub.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finhub.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: TTFT / streaming cadence — FinHub production targets & handoff

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — good discussion. Quick written recap from my side so we have a single reference and clear next steps. Please confirm or correct the numbers below.

Call summary / performance targets (as discussed)
- Primary KPI: 90th percentile Time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target of ~250ms for short responses (<= 200 tokens).
- Long responses (400–1k tokens): acceptable 90p TTFT up to 600ms, but first byte should still stream quickly with progressive chunks.
- Streaming: FinHub prefers server-sent events (SSE) for phase 1. Key requirement is an immediate first chunk (perceptible <300ms) followed by steady chunk cadence—roughly 150–300ms between chunks for bulk text.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline 80 req/s, peak 120 req/s, concurrency target ~60 simultaneous active streams.
- Typical response size: median ~400 tokens; heavy queries up to ~1,200 tokens.
- SLA/ops: target production rollout in Q3 pilot, start with a 2-week pilot load test and a POC afterwards.

Open technical questions for you (please confirm):
1) Do you need WebSocket at any point or is SSE mandatory for phase 1?
2) Any hard constraints on per-connection idle timeouts or corporate proxies that might chunk SSE traffic?
3) Do you want encrypted KV cache of recent prefixes (we can do customer-scoped caching on Dedicated)?

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf (M.A.P. draft), push-architecture.png (rough dataflow).

Proposed next steps
- Please confirm the numbers above (TTFT 90p, throughput, concurrency).
- If yes, we’ll schedule a pilot plan (load window) and a technical pre-check with your infra team.
- Rishi will draft a short test matrix (latency + concurrency scenarios) after confirmation.

Available dates for pilot load test: Jul 27–29 (your TZ). Can you confirm availability?

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TTFT / streaming cadence — FinHub production targets & handoff

Monica — thanks for the tidy summary. Confirming numbers from our side and a couple clarifications: we attached a quick traffic estimate workbook (finhub-traffic-estimates.xlsx).

Confirmed items
- TTFT: primary goal is 90p <= 300ms for short responses (we can accept up to 350ms while optimizing, but prefer target 250–300ms).
- Chunking: we want a visible first chunk as soon as possible (<300ms), subsequent chunk cadence should average ~200–300ms for the first ~2–3 seconds, then can relax to 300–500ms for very long outputs.
- Protocol: SSE only in phase 1 — we have legacy browser clients that depend on EventSource semantics; WebSocket is something we'll consider in phase 2 for mobile/low-latency clients.
- Throughput/concurrency: workbook shows baseline 80–90 req/s with predictable spikes to ~120 req/s for 20–30 mins/day. Concurrency peak of ~60 is the right planning number.
- Typical content length: median ~400–600 tokens; 95p <= 1,200 tokens.

Questions from our infra team
1) Do you have a recommended chunk size by bytes/tokens to minimize reassembly costs on our side?
2) How does Redwood recommend handling keep-alive/connection resets during long streams (we use a corporate proxy that can silently drop idle SSE connections after ~60s)?

Pilot availability
Jul 27–29 works for us; prefer Jul 28 for the main load window.

Thanks —
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering | FinHub
liam.oconnor@finhub.com

Subject: Re: TTFT / streaming cadence — FinHub production targets & handoff

Thanks Liam — perfect, this is super helpful. A few immediate notes and a concrete pilot proposal below.

Quick answers
- Recommended chunk sizing: start with a small initial chunk (~32–128 bytes / ~8–32 tokens) to give instant perceived progress, then use ~256–512 byte chunks (~60–120 tokens) while the model generates the bulk. We’ll provide configuration knobs for chunk targets in the pilot.
- Keep-alive: we suggest two strategies given your corporate proxy constraint: 1) short application-level heartbeats (empty SSE comments) every 30s to keep proxies from idling; 2) graceful client reconnection logic to continue the stream using cursored checkpoints (Redwood supports KV-prefixed resume on Dedicated).

Pilot proposal (Jul 28 main load window)
- Goal: validate 90p TTFT <= 300ms under 80–120 req/s with concurrency up to 60, and confirm chunk cadence under SSE across your proxy.
- Scope: 2-day pre-check (Jul 27) to validate connectivity, and a 6-hour controlled blast on Jul 28 (09:00–15:00 UTC) with scenarios: short responses, medium, long (up to 1,200 tokens), and intermittent spike testing.
- Infra options: we recommend starting on Hosted API with a reserved capacity plan plus burst headroom (fastest to stand up). If the pilot shows sustained demand and you want KV caching + customer-scoped prefix caching, we’ll propose a Dedicated pod for the production roll.
- Success criteria: 90p TTFT <= 300ms for short flows and stable chunk cadence (median inter-chunk 200–300ms) for streaming; no more than 5% of connections dropped by proxy issues (we’ll instrument retries).

Next steps
1) FinHub confirm acceptance of pilot window (Jul 27 pre-check / Jul 28 main load).
2) We’ll send a short M.A.P. (attached) with responsibilities and an invitation for a technical prep call (Rishi + Dev).
3) Rishi to share the test matrix and Redwood load script snippets.

If that looks good I’ll lock Jul 28 and get the invite out.

Best,
Monica Patel

Monica / Dev — quick internal tech note to capture what we’ll run in the pilot. Copying below into the MAP doc.

Test matrix highlights- Latency measurement: measure TTFT at the client edge (FinHub) and at the Redwood ingress. We'll compare 50/90/99p. Target to validate 90p <= 300ms for short flows.
- Chunk cadence: configured initial chunk 64 bytes, follow-ups ~320 bytes. Instrument inter-chunk timings and token counts.
- Connection resilience: heartbeats every 30s (SSE comment: ":heartbeat
") and a resume token approach — client reconnect should include last received offset so we can continue from cached KV position where applicable.
- Scaling: run concurrency ramps 10 -> 30 -> 60. For the burst test, emulate 120 req/s for 30 minutes.
- Observability: enable per-request traces, token-level cost logging, and per-connection drop counters. Rishi will expose dashboards in the console for the FinHub team.

Engineering asks for pilot pre-check
1) Access to a staging EventSource endpoint and one representative corporate proxy config (if you can share).
2) A short staging key we can use for the controlled test.

I’ll draft the load scripts and share in the MAP doc by EOD Jul 21.

-rishi
